title: Mod Scenario – Add Countries
description: Fragment file: defines new countries to introduce in the scenario. Maps to ScenarioCountryDefinition[].

templateISO3.description: ISO3 of an existing country to copy from: its economy, military, AI personality, political starting state and every field this entry leaves out. There is no fully custom country: when omitted, the game falls back to the existing country with the alphabetically first ISO3 (ABW, Aruba, in the base game) and logs a warning, but does not copy that fallback's dominantReligion, dominantEthnicity, primaryCulture or ethnicHomogeneity. Ignored when iso3 already exists (the entry then re-skins that country).

iso3.description: ISO3 code of the new country. Use an ISO3 that no real country has: a code that belongs to a real country the scenario removes or does not play makes the new country inherit that country's 2026 population pyramid and demographic rates (there is no useSeedRow switch), and the game logs a load warning. A code of a base-game country that stays in the scenario re-skins that country instead.

mapColorVibrant.description: Optional vibrant palette variant of mapColor. Falls back to mapColor when absent.

mapColorGloomy.description: Optional gloomy palette variant of mapColor. Falls back to mapColor when absent.

flagPngPath.description: Path to a 128×80 flag PNG. A relative path is looked up in the mod folder (the one holding mod.json) first, then in the scenario folder.

capital.description: Display name of the capital city

capitalProvince.description: Province name or ID string used to resolve the capital entity

militaryUnitTypeIds.description: The country's unit roster. When non-empty the country recruits ONLY these unit types, plus any it owns (units_define ownerIso3); the list may grant another country's exclusive unit. Disabled categories and ids still apply. Empty or omitted keeps the default set.

leaderGender.description: Gender of the starting leader; picks a gender-matched portrait from a portraits/<ISO3>/ bank. When omitted, the first leaderNamePool entry decides (if it has a gender), else the template's.

leaderPortraitPath.description: Mod-relative image (PNG or JPG) shown for the country's STARTING leader instead of the question-mark placeholder, e.g. 'portraits/HYP.png'. Looked up in the mod folder, then the scenario folder, and must stay inside the mod folder: an absolute path or one that climbs out of it is refused. Leaders who take over later use portraits/<ISO3>/<ISO3>_m_01.jpg (or _f_) from the mod folder when present.

leaderNamePool.description: Names this country's later leaders are drawn from, instead of its region's name pool (elections, coups, deaths). The first entry is also the starting leader when leaderName is omitted, so a pool alone replaces the template's leader. A country with a pool and no leaderName/leaderTitle starts with the first entry's name and title.

name.description: Full display name (at most 61 bytes of UTF-8)

title.description: Title this leader carries, e.g. 'Archon' (at most 29 bytes). Blank = the title the government type gives.

gender.description: Picks a gender-matched portrait. Default male.

lockLeaderTitle.description: True keeps leaderTitle on every leader drawn from leaderNamePool, whatever the government type becomes (the game would otherwise retitle them President, Chairman and so on). Needs leaderTitle and a leaderNamePool.

homelandTerm.description: Override the term used for this country's homeland, e.g. 'Federation'

neutral.description: Military neutrality (true/false). Omitted keeps the template country's flag. An AI-controlled neutral forms no military alliances or defense pacts, gives no guarantees, joins no coalitions and answers no calls to arms; a human player is unrestricted.

dominantReligion.description: Largest religion. Two countries with the same label are kin: relations warm, and the AI is slower to attack and quicker to ally. Common base-game labels: Christianity, Islam, Buddhism, Hinduism, Judaism, Shintoism, Sikhism, Taoism, None (non-religious). Any label works and is kin only to the same label; generic labels (None, Other, Mixed, Unknown) are never kin. Omitted keeps the template's value, or stays empty (no kinship) when templateISO3 is omitted. At most 29 bytes of UTF-8 (29 ASCII letters, fewer accented or non-Latin ones); a longer label is cut short with a warning.

dominantEthnicity.description: Largest ethnic group, e.g. 'Turkish'. Same kinship rule as dominantReligion; generic labels (Other, Mixed, None, Unknown, European, ...) are never kin. Omitted keeps the template's value, or stays empty when templateISO3 is omitted. At most 29 bytes of UTF-8 (29 ASCII letters, fewer accented or non-Latin ones); a longer label is cut short with a warning.

primaryCulture.description: Primary culture shown on the country overview, e.g. 'Ottoman'. Omitted keeps the template's value, or stays empty when templateISO3 is omitted. At most 29 bytes of UTF-8 (29 ASCII letters, fewer accented or non-Latin ones); a longer label is cut short with a warning.

ethnicHomogeneity.description: 0 = very diverse, 1 = homogeneous; shown on the country overview when a culture or ethnicity is set. Omitted keeps the template's value, or 0 when templateISO3 is omitted.
